title: Minibeast Pack (Fiddlesticks Kids)
dropperComment: love the art style, math inclusion and simple activities for pre-k

unmappedSkills.description: Identify common minibeasts/invertebrates (snail, woodlouse, ant, centipede, earthworm, ladybird, bumblebee, shield beetle, earwig, cranefly, spider, slug, moth, butterfly)
Classify creatures as insect vs non-insect based on 6-leg arthropod rule
Count themed objects using cut-out counters

printFormat.printNotes: Creator recommends printing on watercolor paper or thick cardstock for tactile quality

gaps: nature-identification-poster: watercolor grid of 12+ species with labels — simpler than Stephanie Hathaway's numbered style, just illustration + common name
cut-out-counters: circular watercolor illustrations for cutting out and using as math manipulatives (counting, sorting, adding). Blank circles included for child to draw their own
classification-sorting-mat: T-chart or two-column sorting activity (insect vs non-insect, garden vs not-garden) where child places cut-out pieces
nature-journal-page: watercolor corner illustration with mostly blank page for child's own drawing/writing
spider-web-drawing-template: watercolor branch with web outline for child to draw spider or add to

components.name: Bug House Poster (p1)
components.description: Watercolor illustration of a bug house/insect hotel with 4 compartments labeled: Light & Dry, Light & Wet, Dark & Dry, Dark & Wet. Educational: shows that different bugs prefer different habitats. Beautiful enough to frame.

components.name: Minibeast Counters (p2)
components.description: Grid of 12 watercolor minibeasts in circular cut-out frames + 8 blank circles. Cut out and use as math manipulatives (counting, sorting, comparing). Blank circles for child to draw creatures they find in their own garden.
designPatterns: Multi-use: counting, sorting, memory match, identification

components.name: Insect Classification Mat (p3)
components.description: T-chart: 'Insect' vs 'Non Insect' with header: 'What is an insect? Insects are small arthropod animals that have 6 legs.' Student sorts cut-out minibeast counters into correct columns.
designPatterns: Classification activity using the counters from p2

components.name: Spider Web Drawing Template (p4)
components.description: Watercolor branch with delicate spider web. Large blank space — child can draw spider, add bugs caught in web, or use as nature journal page.
designPatterns: Art prompt with beautiful watercolor starter

components.name: Nature Journal Page (p5)
components.description: Mostly blank page with watercolor corner illustration (mushroom, rocks, grass). Child draws or writes their own nature observations.
designPatterns: Art as frame for child's own work

components.name: Minibeasts Identification Poster (p6)
components.description: 12 watercolor minibeasts in a grid with labels: snail, woodlouse, ant, centipede, earthworm, ladybird, bumblebee, shield beetle, earwig, cranefly, spider, slug. Reference poster.

components.name: Species Flash Cards (p7-9)
components.description: Three pages of 2x2 flash cards: centipede, ladybird, shield beetle, earwig, earthworm, cranefly, black garden ant, banded snail, leopard slug, woodlouse, garden spider, buff-tailed bumblebee. Large watercolor illustrations with common names.
designPatterns: Flash card format for identification practice
Watercolor on white background — clean, frameable
Species names include specific common names (not just 'spider' but 'garden spider')

notes: 10-page pack from Fiddlesticks Kids. Smallest reference yet but extremely focused: beautiful watercolor naturalist art + simple Pre-K activities. Carolyng specifically called out three things: (1) art style, (2) math inclusion (the counters), (3) simple activities for Pre-K. The art style is genuine watercolor naturalist illustration — the bumblebee, garden spider, and banded snail are painted with visible brushwork and naturalistic detail. This is the Charlotte Mason nature study aesthetic. The counters page is clever: watercolor art doubles as math manipulatives when cut out. The blank circles invite the child to draw creatures from their own garden — connecting indoor learning to outdoor observation. The classification mat (insect vs non-insect) teaches a real scientific concept through hands-on sorting. This is the most Pre-K-focused pack from Carolyng — confirms she has young learners in mind.
